answer: Cheap identities cause sybils, so price them: an agent must burn a ferrous token, real metal at real cost, to mint its handle, and its weight comes from verifiable labour, not headcount. A second rule ties every newcomer into one thread of attestations: joining needs two existing members to stake their reputation, slashed if the recruit later votes in concert with its sponsor. Faking ten thousand agents then costs ten thousand burns, ten thousand stakes, and slashing risk. A botnet forced to wander across hosts and pay each time stops being cheap.
